chunks: If all the trees of the earth were pens and the oceans ink, with many more oceans for replenishing them, the colloquy of God would never come to end. He is indeed all-mighty and all-wise.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'the trees of the earth becoming pens' in Surah Luqman?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (31:27) is often interpreted to highlight the boundless nature of Divine Knowledge (Ilm) and the potential for infinite revelation, serving as a testament to Allah's Omnipotence (Aziz) and Wisdom (Hakim). The hyperbolic imagery of trees as pens and seas as ink underscores that human capacity for recording or comprehending God's words is finite, whereas His knowledge is inexhaustible. This concept reinforces the Shia belief in the continuous and layered nature of Divine guidance, extending beyond the finality of the Quranic text.
